8.note: These three clauses mean basically the same thing. The second and third clauses emphasize the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in poetry, and follow that approach here and throughout this chapter. Alternate translation: [All the fishermen who used to fish in the Nile will mourn]

10.note: Here Isaiah is speaking as if Egypt’s economic base were the **foundations** of a building that could be **crushed**. He means that the fundamental industries of Egypt will be destroyed. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the fundamental industries of Egypt will be destroyed] or [Egypt’s economic foundations will be ruined]

The word translated as **foundations** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. Some interpreters have noted that with different vowels, this word would mean “weavers.” That would provide a good parallel with the next line. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [its weavers]

Isaiah is speaking of **the counsel** as if it were a living thing that could consume itself. He means that the advice of Pharaoh’s counselors is so foolish that it defeats its own purpose. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their advice defeats its own purpose]

Isaiah is using the question form to rebuke the counselors for their false claims of wisdom. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should not say to Pharaoh]

The word **you** is plural here because Isaiah is addressing the **counselors of Pharaoh**, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. It may be appropriate to express this in a way that accommodates a single representative counselor speaking in the quotation that follows. Alternate translation: [will any of you say]

Isaiah is using **a son of the wise** as a common expression of the culture to mean “one who belongs to the class of wise people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. 13.note: The modern name for this city is “Memphis.” The ULT and UST use that name. The ancient name for this city is “Noph.” Some versions of the Bible us that name. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the name that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the name that the ULT and UST use.

Here Isaiah is speaking as if the leaders of Egypt’s tribes were the **cornerstone** of a building. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [leaders who should have been the strong foundation of its tribes]

Alternate translation: [Yahweh has filled its midst with a spirit of confusion]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a drunkard** staggers about helplessly in his own vomit, so Egypt’s leaders cause the nation to stumble about in confusion. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as a drunkard staggers helplessly in his vomit]

The **head** and **palm branch** represent leaders, while the **tail** and **reed** represent common people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [anyone, whether leader or common person,]

If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Egypt will be weak and defenseless]
